inputs.text: [excited][playful] Here we are in the [serious] Ice Age! [happily] Later on, the cold comes back. [serious] Really cold. [gasps] Ice covers the continents for millions of years.
[playful][happily] A lot! [excited] Ice spreads over Europe and North America. [softly] The animals adapt: thick fur, fat under the skin.
[excited][quickly] The woolly mammoth, a cousin of the elephant, with fur all the way down to its feet! [happily] The saber-toothed cat. Wolves. Cave bears.

[happily][excited] Yes! [gasps] About two and a half million years ago, in Africa, the first humans appear. [playful] They walk upright, and they eat a bit of everything: plants, fruit, seeds, meat. [softly] They're hunter-gatherers.
[playful][happily] Not quite! [excited] About three hundred thousand years ago, Homo sapiens shows up. [gasps] That's our direct ancestor: humans just like us.
[excited][quickly] Humans get really clever. [happily] They make fire, they talk, they make sharp tools. [softly] They hunt big animals and protect themselves from the cold.
[happily][excited] The kings of the planet! [gasps] The ultimate hunters. [quickly] They raise animals, grow plants, build villages, cities, roads, bridges, boats.
[excited][quickly] Even more! [gasps] They invent electricity, the steam engine, the motor. [happily] The car, the train, the bicycle, the telephone.
[excited][quickly] And they fly! [happily] In hot-air balloons, in planes, in rockets. [softly] Humans learn to master animals, nature, and the forces of physics.
[softly][happily] We're almost at today. [pauses] Ready to find out [curious] how we know all this?
